question: What is the difference between a somatic cell and a reproductive cell?

options.text: Somatic cells undergo mitotic cell division while reproductive cells undergo meiotic cell division.
The somatic cells have mitochondria but the reproductive cells do not have any mitochondria.
Somatic cells do not contain any chromosome while reproductive cells have their own chromosome.
The somatic cell and reproductive cell are neither diploid nor haploid.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Somatic cells** undergo mitotic cell division, while **reproductive cells** undergo meiotic cell division.
 
• Somatic cells are **diploid** (having two sets of chromosomes), whereas reproductive cells (gametes) are **haploid** (having one set of chromosomes).
 
• Somatic cells make up most of the body's tissues and organs, while reproductive cells are involved in sexual reproduction.
 
• During mitosis, somatic cells produce identical daughter cells, maintaining the chromosome number, whereas meiosis in reproductive cells results in four non-identical daughter cells with half the chromosome number.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Somatic cells include cells of the skin, liver, lungs, etc., while reproductive cells include sperm and egg cells.
 
• Errors in mitosis can lead to conditions such as cancer, whereas errors in meiosis can result in genetic disorders such as Down syndrome.
 
• Both types of cells contain mitochondria, and both types have chromosomes, though their chromosome numbers and types of division differ.
